messages.subject: Besag/BYM including observations without neighbours
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to fit a model to areal data (property-level observations) and wish to account for spatial autocorrelation, which I have opted to do with a 'bym2' term. Due to the nature of the properties I am analysing, very few have shared boundaries, but many of them are within very close proximity of eachother (just not contiguous). Therefore, I've created a distance matrix containing the pair wise minimum distances between all properties, and have binarised this matrix based on a series of candidate thresholds (e.g., 100m, 250m, 500m and so on), where properties are considered neighbours (1 value in the binarised matrix) if they are less than x metres apart. 

My issue arises due to the fact that under this methodology, some observations (properties) do not have any neighbours. I have been using spdep to convert the distance matrix to a 'nb' list and then trying to use the 'nb2INLA' function to convert this to an INLA-readable graph file - however, the function gives the error 'Error in card(nb) : zero length neighbour vector'. To my understanding, the 'besag'/'bym' models implemented in INLA can deal with observations not having any neighbours, but I'm wondering if there are any special steps I need to take to create a suitable graph file in these circumstances? And do I need to add any additional specifications to the bym2 random effect call? At the moment I am just using: 

f(ID, model = 'bym2', scale.model = T, constr = T, graph = my_graph)

and have got the model to run succesfully when using an adjacency matrix based on k-nearest neighbours (so each observation always has at least 1 neighbour). 

Thanks for any help,

Ciar

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Besag/BYM including observations without neighbours
parts:
I think there might be issues with k-nearest neighbours, that its not symmetric,
that is if 'i' is in the set of the k-nearest neighb of 'j', then 'j' is not
necessary in the set of k-nearest neighbh of 'i'.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Besag/BYM including observations without neighbours
parts:
Sorry, perhaps I wasn't entirely clear. I have succesfully got this model to run when using k-nearest neighbours, as I specified:

centroids <- st_point_on_surface(props)
prop_nns <- knearneigh(centroids, k = 4)
nn_ngbs <- knn2nb(prop_nns, row.names = props$ID, sym = T)

The issue with this is, I end up with some properties being considered neighbours that are actually very far apart (>5 km). So, I instead am trying to create an adjacency matrix where properties are only considered neighbours if they are < say 500 m (I intend to use WAIC to compare a series of different distance thresholds). When I do this, I end up with some properties having 0 neighbours. Conceptually, this is fine for my purposes, but I'm wondering if it is possible to use a bym2 model when some observations do not have any neighbours? And if so, how do I structure the graph file, as nb2INLA will not allow me to converte a nb object to a graph when any of the neighbour vectors have length 0.
